 State of Odisha .... Opposite Party(s)
 Mr. B. K. Ragada, Aga
 Coram: Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra

Order 
16.05.2024 Order No.
02. 1. Heard.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in F.I.R. dated 01.11.2017 in Badambadi P.S. Case No.292 of 2017 for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 294 and 506 of I.P.C. read with Section 67 of the Information Technology Act and facing the trial.

3. The Petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated 19.07.2022 passed by the learned 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Cuttack in S.T. Case No.328 of 2019, whereby the application of the prosecution to allow the victim (P.W.4) to produce four Compact Discs (C.D.) has been allowed.
The Petitioner has taken nude photographs and video of the victim and threatened to viral those videos.
Using three different mobile numbers, the Petitioner has also threatened the victim, which has been recorded by the victim and converted to an audio C.D.
The victim (P.W.4) wants to produce those C.Ds during the trial.
Hence, the prayer was made for accepting those C.Ds in evidence by the prosecution.

The learned trial Court while dealing with the application observed as under:-
<Perused the case record.

The accused is facing trial for the offence u/ss/
376(2)(n)/506/354-C/201/294 I.P.C. read with Section 67/67(A) I.T. Act.
The witnesses examined so far including the victim (P.W.4) have stated that the accused threatened the victim to make viral of her nude photos and videos.
PW-4 has stated that by giving such threat, the accused kept physical relationship with her.
The accused is also charged for the offence u/s. 506/294/201 of IPC read with Section 67/67A of I.T. Act for which the alleged C.Ds are relevant for just decision of this case.
On perusal of the case record, it is found that the victim has yet not produced those C.Ds in Court.
Hence, the prayer of the learned Addl. P.P. is allowed.

1 is directed to produce those four C.Ds in Court which shall be accepted in evidence subject to the law guiding production and admissibility of electronic record.=

sentences.text: For the reasons recorded in the order, the application of the prosecution has been allowed and C.Ds was directed to be brought on record for just decision of the case.
The Petitioner who is the accused in the case is aggrieved and assails the same in this petition.

4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that the said C.Ds were neither produced by the police during investigation nor the victim has stated at any point of time regarding the existence of those C.Ds.
The C.Ds are sought to be indirectly brought on record without being resorting to the provision of Section 91 or Section 293 Cr.P.C.
In any case the said provisions could only be exercisable by the Court and the prosecution cannot move such application.
5. Mr. Ragada, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State submits that vide common impugned order, the learned trial Court has allowed the application of the Petitioner to recall P.W.4.
Therefore, the Petitioner has an option for confronting the victim (P.W.4) with the said C.Ds.
The I.O. of the case has also not been examined as yet.

The Petitioner has a right to confront the I.O.
with the C.D., which has been brought on record.
That precisely the reason, the learned trial Court has allowed the application of the petitioner to recall the victim (P.W.4).
Therefore, there is no prejudice likely to cause to the Petitioner.
6. I agree with the contention made by Mr. Ragada, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and found that the impugned order does not suffer with any legal infirmity.

The learned trial Court has allowed the C.Ds to be brought on record for just decision of the case and also protected the right of the Petitioner by recalling the victim (P.W.4) by the impugned order.
The order impugned being a balanced order without prejudice to either party, I am not inclined to interfere and entertain this petition.
7. Accordingly, the CRLMC is dismissed.

(S.S. Mishra) Judge Swarna Location: High Court of Orissa Anand Jena vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party(S) on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105949938/
